projectSummary: In vivo mechanical evidence that the regions of the pectoralis major behave differently as the humerus is moved. Combined with the regional activation and moment-arm evidence, this is why the muscle page treats the muscle as regionally differentiated rather than uniform.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: Abstract-only, male participants only, passive rather than active behaviour.

study.intervention: In vivo shear-wave elastography of pectoralis major regions during passive shoulder rotation.
study.population: Shear wave elastography assessed the stretch response of different pectoralis major regions during shoulder abduction and external rotation in 20 healthy male participants; the shoulder was passively rotated through range in 5.7-degree increments and shear wave velocity was obtained for each region, then fitted with a piecewise model giving slack angle, slack stiffness and elasticity coefficient.

title: The in vivo passive stretch response of the pectoralis major is region-specific.
